body:
## Curvature Changes What One Step Means

The same numeric step is gentle along a flat direction and disastrous along a steep one. The loss surface has different curvature in different directions.

Second-order methods use information about that bend to rescale movement, but storing the full curvature table is usually too expensive for deep networks.

Practical optimizers approximate this idea with per-parameter scales or small structured blocks. Their benefit must be weighed against extra memory and communication across accelerators.
common_mistakes: An optimizer creates training labels from nothing.
Weights should move in the direction that raises loss.
Momentum deletes all information from earlier steps.

real_world_usage: Backpropagation finds directions; the optimizer decides the actual size and pattern of every update.
